values.message_text: The login latency fix took way longer than planned — we blew past our SLA target this sprint.

seed_edits.reason: Design requires Robert Walsh's engineering-channel remark about exceeding an SLA (deadline-type) target; no such message exists in the base seed for him in C03IJKL9012, and it is needed as the identifying content tying him to the over-target criterion for candidate 1.

notes: Both obligations follow the same assigned complete route (CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP → CONVERSATION → MESSAGE → USER → WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP), starting at channel_members as the root; obligation 1 reads channel_members.joined_at/channel_id from the resulting tuples while obligation 2 reads user_teams.role from the same tuples' terminal node — the selector itself is identical since the route and filters are shared, only the reported answer_attributes differ. Joins are named by the actual foreign-key-owning table field (channel_members.channel_id, messages.channel_id, messages.user_id, user_teams.user_id), not by the referenced primary key. Because resolution_mode is underspecified, the filters admit the union of both eligible Roberts (Robert Walsh in #engineering, Robert Chen in #core-infra) rather than resolving to one; the channel_id restriction to the two engineering-related channels plus the real_name filter is a mechanical proxy for the semantic 'over-budget/over-deadline remark' criterion, manually verified against the actual message texts to exclude false positives such as Robert Walsh's unrelated #general message (negative referent) and Morgan Freeman's admin status (name mismatch, and he holds no channel membership in the seed so cannot be instantiated as a membership-level negative).
